title: حِكَايَةُ التَّاجِرِ وَأَوْلَادِهِ
titleEn: The Merchant and His Sons, continued
part: Night 40 · The Merchant and His Sons, continued
source: William Hay Macnaghten, ed., The Alif Laila, or Book of the Thousand Nights and One Night, vol. 1, Calcutta 1839 (“Calcutta II”), printed pp. 327–332 (Night 40, continuing directly from nights-39), transcribed from the 300 ppi scan (archive.org aliflailaorbooko01macn) by the editors' own transcription. The edition prints the prose essentially unpointed: ALL VOCALIZATION (tashkīl) IS EDITORIAL — ours, not the edition's — and the alphabet button strips it back to the bare rasm exactly as Macnaghten prints it. Romanization is simplified IJMES. Spelling, including the edition's Middle Arabic forms and its occasional compositor's slips, is preserved unaltered; a few genuinely obscure or corrupt-looking forms are vocalized by evident sense and flagged in the notes rather than silently repaired. Read-aloud audio is a Modern Standard Arabic reading of this vocalised text, synthesized by machine, with word-by-word timing generated the same way.
about: Night 40 concludes the second slave Kāfūr's tale — the slave who tells one lie a year, and how his master's revenge made him a eunuch — and the third slave puts off his own until morning. The slaves bury the chest and go; at dawn Ghānim ibn Ayyūb digs it up, breaks it open and finds a drugged girl, who wakes, learns what has happened, and asks to be carried to his house. Shahrazād is overtaken by morning at the moment the chest is opened. As with every printed edition of the Nights, this one belongs to the late Egyptian recension (ZER) — an eighteenth-century expansion padded out to a literal 1001 nights; no printed edition is a medieval text, and Macnaghten regularised the language here and there, so some Middle Arabic texture is a nineteenth-century retrofit.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَانَتِ اللَّيْلَةُ الْمُوفِيَةُ لِلْأَرْبَعِينَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kānati al-laylatu al-mūfiyatu li-al-arbaʿīna
sentences.l: And-when came-to-be the-night, the-completing-one of-the-forty,
sentences.i: When the fortieth night came,

sentences.t: قَالَتْ بَلَغَنِي أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ السَّعِيدُ أَنَّهُمْ لَمَّا وَصَلُوا إِلَى الْوَالِي وَأَخْبَرُوهُ قَامَ الْوَالِي وَرَكِبَ وَأَخَذَ مَعَهُ الْفَعَلَةَ بِالْمَسَاحِي وَالْقُفَفِ
sentences.tr: qālat balaghanī ayyuhā al-maliku al-saʿīdu annahum lammā waṣalū ilā al-wālī wa-akhbarūhu qāma al-wālī wa-rakiba wa-akhadha maʿahu al-faʿalata bi-al-masāḥī wa-al-qufafi
sentences.l: She-said: It-has-reached-me, O the-king the-fortunate, that-they, when they-arrived at the-governor and-informed-him, rose the-governor and-mounted and-took with-him the-workmen with-the-hoes and-the-baskets,
sentences.i: She said: It has reached me, O fortunate king, that when they came to the governor and told him, the governor rose, mounted, and took with him the labourers, equipped with hoes and baskets,

sentences.t: وَمَشَوْا تَابِعِينَ أَثَرِي وَمَعَهُمْ كَثِيرٌ مِنَ النَّاسِ وَأَنَا قُدَّامَهُمْ أَلْطِمُ عَلَى وَجْهِي وَأَصِيحُ
sentences.tr: wa-mashaw tābiʿīna atharī wa-maʿahum kathīrun mina al-nāsi wa-anā quddāmahum alṭimu ʿalā wajhī wa-aṣīḥu
sentences.l: And-they-walked, following my-track, and-with-them many of the-people, and-I before-them slapping on my-face and-crying-out,
sentences.i: and they walked on, following in my track, with a great crowd of people beside them, while I ran ahead of them, slapping my face and crying out,
sentences.n: قدام (quddām, “in front of”) is the colloquial form of classical قُدَّامَ; common in this text.

sentences.t: وَسِتِّي وَأَوْلَادُهَا خَلْفِي يَعِيطُونَ
sentences.tr: wa-sittī wa-awlāduhā khalfī yaʿīṭūna
sentences.l: and-my-lady and-her-children behind-me, wailing.
sentences.i: and my mistress and her children came behind me, wailing.
sentences.n: ستي (sitt, “lady, mistress”) is colloquial; يعيطون (yaʿīṭūn) is the colloquial verb for “to cry out, wail”, here in place of classical يصيحون.

sentences.t: فَجَرَيْتُ أَنَا قُدَّامَهُمْ وَسَبَقْتُهُمْ وَأَنَا أَصِيحُ وَأَحْثُو التُّرَابَ عَلَى رَأْسِي وَأَلْطِمُ عَلَى وَجْهِي
sentences.tr: fa-jaraytu anā quddāmahum wa-sabaqtuhum wa-anā aṣīḥu wa-aḥthū al-turāba ʿalā raʾsī wa-alṭimu ʿalā wajhī
sentences.l: So-I-ran, I, before-them, and-outstripped-them, and-I crying-out and-throwing the-dust on my-head and-slapping on my-face,
sentences.i: I ran on ahead of them and outstripped them, crying out, throwing dust on my head and slapping my face,

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا دَخَلْتُ الْبُسْتَانَ وَرَآنِي سَيِّدِي وَأَنَا أَلْطِمُ وَأَقُولُ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā dakhaltu al-bustāna wa-raʾānī sayyidī wa-anā alṭimu wa-aqūlu
sentences.l: And-when I-entered the-garden and-saw-me my-master, and-I slapping and-saying:
sentences.i: and when I entered the garden, my master saw me slapping myself and saying:

sentences.t: وَاسِتَّاهْ ا وَاءْ ا وَاهْ أَوَّاهْ
sentences.tr: wā-sittāh ā wāʾ ā wāh awwāh
sentences.l: O my-lady! Ah! Woe! Ah! Alas! Oh!
sentences.n: A string of cries of grief. The print gives the bare interjections ا، واء، ا، واه، اواه; the vocalisation of the unattached ا and of واء is conjectural.

sentences.t: مَنْ بَقِيَ لِي يَحِنُّ عَلَيَّ بَعْدَ سَيِّدَتِى
sentences.tr: man baqiya lī yaḥinnu ʿalayya baʿda sayyidatī
sentences.l: Who has-remained for-me, who-would-feel-tenderness for me after my-mistress?
sentences.i: Who is left to feel for me, now that my mistress is gone?

sentences.t: يَا لَيْتَنِي كُنْتُ فِدَاءً عَنْهَا
sentences.tr: yā laytanī kuntu fidāʾan ʿanhā
sentences.l: O would-that-I had-been a ransom on-behalf-of her!
sentences.i: If only I had been the ransom for her!

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا رَآنِي سَيِّدِي بَهِتَ وَاصْفَرَّ لَوْنُهُ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā raʾānī sayyidī bahita wa-iṣfarra lawnuhu
sentences.l: And-when saw-me my-master, he-was-dumbfounded and-turned-yellow his-colour,
sentences.i: When my master saw me, he stood stunned and his face went yellow,
sentences.n: بهت is read bahita, “was dumbfounded”; بُهِتَ (“was confounded”) is also possible.

sentences.t: وَقَالَ مَالَكَ يَا كَافُورُ وَمَا الْخَبَرُ
sentences.tr: wa-qāla mā-laka yā Kāfūru wa-mā al-khabaru
sentences.l: and-he-said: What-to-you, O Kāfūr, and-what the-news?
sentences.i: and said: What is wrong, Kāfūr? What is the news?

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ لَهُ إِنَّكَ لَمَّا أَرْسَلْتَنِي إِلَى الْبَيْتِ وَدَخَلْتُ فَرَأَيْتُ الْحَائِطَ الَّتِي فِى الْقَاعَةِ وَقَعَتْ وَانْطَبَقَتْ كُلُّهَا عَلَى سِتِّي وَأَوْلَادِهَا
sentences.tr: fa-qultu lahu innaka lammā arsaltanī ilā al-bayti wa-dakhaltu fa-raʾaytu al-ḥāʾiṭa allatī fī al-qāʿati waqaʿat wa-inṭabaqat kulluhā ʿalā sittī wa-awlādihā
sentences.l: So-I-said to-him: Indeed-you, when you-sent-me to the-house and-I-entered, I-saw the-wall (f.) which is-in the-hall: it-fell and-closed-over, all-of-it, upon my-lady and-her-children.
sentences.i: So I said to him: When you sent me to the house and I went in, I saw that the wall in the hall had fallen and collapsed, all of it, on my mistress and her children.
sentences.n: حائط (wall) is treated as feminine here (التي ... وقعت ... كلها), as classical usage allows.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لِي وَهَلْ سِتُّكَ مَا سَلِمَتْ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lī wa-hal sittuka mā salimat
sentences.l: So-he-said to-me: And-did your-lady not escape?
sentences.i: He said to me: And did your mistress not escape?

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ لَهُ لَا وَاللَّهِ يَا سَيِّدِي مَا سَلِمَ مِنْهُمْ أَحَدٌ
sentences.tr: fa-qultu lahu lā wa-Allāhi yā sayyidī mā salima minhum aḥadun
sentences.l: So-I-said to-him: No, by-God, O my-master, not escaped of-them anyone.
sentences.i: I said to him: No, by God, my master, not one of them escaped.

sentences.t: وَأَوَّلُ مَنْ مَاتَ مِنْهُمْ سِتِّي الْكَبِيرَةُ
sentences.tr: wa-awwalu man māta minhum sittī al-kabīratu
sentences.l: And-the-first who died of-them was my-lady the-elder.
sentences.i: The first of them to die was my elder mistress.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ وَهَلْ سَلِمَتْ بِنْتِي الصَّغِيرَةُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla wa-hal salimat bintī al-ṣaghīratu
sentences.l: So-he-said: And-did escape my-daughter the-little-one?
sentences.i: He said: And has my little daughter survived?

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ لَهُ لَا
sentences.tr: fa-qultu lahu lā
sentences.l: So-I-said to-him: No.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لِي وَمَاحَالُ الْبَغْلَةِ الَّتِي أَرْكَبُهَا هَلْ هِيَ سَالِمَةٌ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lī wa-māḥālu al-baghlati allatī arkabuhā hal hiya sālimatun
sentences.l: So-he-said to-me: And-what-state-of the-mule which I-ride, is-she safe?
sentences.i: He said to me: And how is the mule I ride? Is she unharmed?
sentences.n: The print joins وما and حال into one word.

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ لَهُ لَا وَاللَّهِ يَا سَيِّدِي فَإِنَّ حِيطَانَ الْبَيْتِ وَحِيطَانَ الْإِصْطَبْلِ انْطَبَقَتْ عَلَى جَمِيعِ مَا فِى الْبَيْتِ حَتَّى عَلَى الْغَنَمِ وَالْأَوَزِّو الدَّجَاجِ
sentences.tr: fa-qultu lahu lā wa-Allāhi yā sayyidī fa-inna ḥīṭāna al-bayti wa-ḥīṭāna al-iṣṭabli inṭabaqat ʿalā jamīʿi mā fī al-bayti ḥattā ʿalā al-ghanami wa-al-awazzi wa-al-dajāji
sentences.l: So-I-said to-him: No, by-God, O my-master, for the-walls of-the-house and-the-walls of-the-stable closed-over upon all that is in the-house, even upon the-sheep and-the-geese, and the-chickens.
sentences.i: I said to him: No, by God, my master. The walls of the house and the walls of the stable have collapsed on everything in the house, even on the sheep, the geese and the chickens,
sentences.n: The print has والاوزّو الدجاج, with a shadda on the zāy and a stray و; the sense is clearly “and the geese and the chickens”, and the و has slipped from before الدجاج. Kept as printed.

sentences.t: وَصَارُوا كُلُّهُمْ كُومَ لَحْمٍ وَأَكَلَهُمُ الْكِلَابُ وَلَمْ يَبْقَ مِنْهُمْ أَحَدٌ
sentences.tr: wa-ṣārū kulluhum kūma laḥmin wa-akalahumu al-kilābu wa-lam yabqa minhum aḥadun
sentences.l: and-they-became, all-of-them, a-heap of-flesh, and-ate-them the-dogs, and-not remained of-them anyone.
sentences.i: and all of them became a heap of meat; the dogs ate them, and not one of them was left.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لِي وَلَا سَيِّدُكَ الْكَبِيرُ سَلِمَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lī wa-lā sayyiduka al-kabīru salima
sentences.l: So-he-said to-me: And-not your-master the-elder escaped?
sentences.i: He said to me: And did your elder master not escape either?

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ لَهُ لَا وَاللَّهِ لَمْ يَسْلَمْ مِنْهُمْ أَحَدٌ
sentences.tr: fa-qultu lahu lā wa-Allāhi lam yaslam minhum aḥadun
sentences.l: So-I-said to-him: No, by-God, did-not escape of-them anyone.
sentences.i: I said to him: No, by God, not one of them escaped.

sentences.t: وَفِي هَذِهِ السَّاعَةِ لَا بَقِيَ دَارٌ وَلَا سُكَّانٌ وَلَا بَقِيَ لَهُمْ أَثَرٌ
sentences.tr: wa-fī hādhihi al-sāʿati lā baqiya dārun wa-lā sukkānun wa-lā baqiya lahum atharun
sentences.l: And-in this the-hour not remained a-house nor inhabitants, and-not remained to-them a-trace.
sentences.i: Even now no house remains, nor any inhabitants, nor any trace of them.

sentences.t: وَأَمَّا الْغَنَمُ وَالْأَوَزُّ وَالدَّجَاجُ فَأَكَلَهُمُ الْقِطَطُ وَالْكِلَابُ
sentences.tr: wa-ammā al-ghanamu wa-al-awazzu wa-al-dajāju fa-akalahumu al-qiṭaṭu wa-al-kilābu
sentences.l: And-as-for the-sheep and-the-geese and-the-chickens, the-cats and-the-dogs ate-them.
sentences.i: As for the sheep, the geese and the chickens, the cats and the dogs devoured them.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ سَيِّدِي كَلَامِي صَارَ الضِّيَاءُ فِى وَجْهِهِ ظَلَامًا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa sayyidī kalāmī ṣāra al-ḍiyāʾu fī wajhihi ẓalāman
sentences.l: And-when heard my-master my-speech, became the-light in his-face darkness.
sentences.i: When my master heard my words, the light in his face turned to darkness.

sentences.t: وَلَمْ يَقْدِرْ يَتَمَالَكُ نَفْسَهُ ، وَلَا عَقْلَهُ
sentences.tr: wa-lam yaqdir yatamālaku nafsahu , wa-lā ʿaqlahu
sentences.l: and-he-was-not-able he-could-hold himself, nor his-wits,
sentences.i: and he could not hold himself together, nor his wits,
sentences.n: Here يقدر is followed directly by the indicative يتمالك, without أن; this is colloquial syntax. The print has a comma before ولا.

sentences.t: وَلَمْ يَقْدِرْأَنْ يَقِفَ عَلَى قَدَمَيْهِ
sentences.tr: wa-lam yaqdir an yaqifa ʿalā qadamayhi
sentences.l: and-he-was-not-able that he-stand on his-two-feet,
sentences.i: and could not stand on his feet,
sentences.n: The print runs يقدر and أن together as يقدران; read as two words.

sentences.t: بَلْ جَاءَ الْكُسَاحُ وَانْكَسَرَ ظَهْرُهُ
sentences.tr: bal jāʾa al-kusāḥu wa-inkasara ẓahruhu
sentences.l: rather came the-lameness and-broke his-back.
sentences.i: rather, a lameness came over him and his back gave way.

sentences.t: وَخَرَقَ أَثْوَابَهُ وَنَنَفَ ذَقْنَهُ وَرَمَى عِمَامَتَهُ مِنْ فَوْقِ رَأْسِهِ
sentences.tr: wa-kharaqa athwābahu wa-nanafa dhaqnahu wa-ramā ʿimāmatahu min fawqi raʾsihi
sentences.l: He-tore his-garments and-plucked his-beard and-threw his-turban from above his-head,
sentences.i: He tore his clothes, plucked at his beard and flung his turban from his head,
sentences.n: ننف is obscure; the sense “plucked” suggests a slip for نتف (natafa) or a doubled form of نَفَّ; it is read here as nanafa.

sentences.t: وَلَازَالَ يَلْطِمُ عَلَى وَجْهِهِ حَتَّى سَالَ مِنْهُ الدَّمُ
sentences.tr: wa-lāzāla yalṭimu ʿalā wajhihi ḥattā sāla minhu al-damu
sentences.l: and-did-not-cease slapping on his-face until flowed from-him the-blood,
sentences.i: and he kept slapping his face until the blood ran from it,
sentences.n: The print joins ولا and زال.

sentences.t: وَصَاحَ آهْ وَا أَوْلَادَاهْ آهْ وَازَوْجَتَاهْ آهْ وَامُصِيبَتَاهْ
sentences.tr: wa-ṣāḥa āh wā-awlādāh āh wā-zawjatāh āh wā-muṣībatāh
sentences.l: and-he-cried-out: Ah! O my-children! Ah! O my-wife! Ah! O my-calamity!
sentences.i: and cried out: Ah, my children! Ah, my wife! Ah, what a disaster!

sentences.t: مَنْ جَرَى لَهُ مِثْلُ مَا جَرَى لِي
sentences.tr: man jarā lahu mithlu mā jarā lī
sentences.l: To-whom has-happened the-like of what happened to-me?
sentences.i: Has anything like what has befallen me ever befallen anyone?

sentences.t: فَصَاحَتِ التُّجَّارُ رُفَقَاؤُهُ لِصِيَاحِهِ وَبَكَوْا مَعَهُ
sentences.tr: fa-ṣāḥati al-tujjāru rufaqāʾuhu li-ṣiyāḥihi wa-bakaw maʿahu
sentences.l: And-cried-out (f.) the-merchants, his-companions, at-his-crying-out, and-they-wept with-him,
sentences.i: His fellow merchants cried out at his cry and wept with him,
sentences.n: The verb صاحت is feminine singular before a plural subject, as is common in the Nights.

sentences.t: وَرَثَوْالِحَالِهِ وَشَقُّوا أَثْوَا بِهِمْ
sentences.tr: wa-rathaw li-ḥālihi wa-shaqqū athwā bihim
sentences.l: and-they-pitied his-state and-tore their-garments,
sentences.i: pitied his state and tore their clothes,
sentences.n: The print joins ورثوا and لحاله, and splits اثوابهم as اثوا بهم; both are kept as printed.

sentences.t: وَخَرَجَ سَيِّدِي مِنْ ذَلِكَ الْبُسْتَانِ وَهُوَ يَلْطِمُ مِنْ شِدَّةِ مَا جَرَى لَهُ
sentences.tr: wa-kharaja sayyidī min dhālika al-bustāni wa-huwa yalṭimu min shiddati mā jarā lahu
sentences.l: and-went-out my-master from that the-garden, and-he slapping from the-severity of-what befell him,
sentences.i: and my master left that garden, slapping himself in the violence of his grief,

sentences.t: وَمِنْ شِدَّةِ اللَّطْمِ عَلَى وَجْهِهِ صَارَ كَأَنَّهُ سَكْرَانُ
sentences.tr: wa-min shiddati al-laṭmi ʿalā wajhihi ṣāra ka-annahu sakrānu
sentences.l: and from the-severity of-the-slapping on his-face he-became as-if-he a-drunk.
sentences.i: and from the force of the blows to his face he became like a drunken man.

sentences.t: فَبَيْنَمَا هُوَ وَالتُّجَّارُ خَارِجُونَ مِنْ بَابِ الْبُسْتَانِ وَإِذَا هُمْ بِغَبْرَةٍ عَظِيمَةٍ وَصِيَاحٍ وَعِيَاطٍ
sentences.tr: fa-baynamā huwa wa-al-tujjāru khārijūna min bābi al-bustāni wa-idhā hum bi-ghabratin ʿaẓīmatin wa-ṣiyāḥin wa-ʿiyāṭin
sentences.l: And-while he and-the-merchants were-going-out from the-gate of-the-garden, and-behold they, with-a-great dust-cloud and-shouting and-clamour,
sentences.i: As he and the merchants were going out of the garden gate, suddenly they met a great cloud of dust, with shouting and uproar.
sentences.n: عياط (ʿiyāṭ, “clamour”) is the colloquial noun from the same root as يعيطون above.

sentences.t: فَنَظَرُوا إِلَى هَؤُلَاءِ الْمُقْبِلِينَ فَإِذَا هُوَ الْوَالِى وَالْمُقَدَّمِينَ وَالْخَلْقُ وَالْعَالَمُ الَّذِينَ يَتَفَرَّجُونَ
sentences.tr: fa-naẓarū ilā hāʾulāʾi al-muqbilīna fa-idhā huwa al-wālī wa-al-muqaddamīna wa-al-khalqu wa-al-ʿālamu alladhīna yatafarrajūna
sentences.l: So-they-looked at these the-approaching-ones, and-behold, it-was the-governor and-the-officers and-the-folk and-the-world who were-looking-on,
sentences.i: They looked at those who were approaching, and it was the governor, with his officers and a crowd of onlookers,
sentences.n: المقدمين is accusative/genitive where classical grammar would have the nominative المقدمون after هو الوالي; the text is loose here. “The folk and the world” (الخلق والعالم) is an idiom for “everybody”.

sentences.t: وَأَهْلُ التَّاجِرِ وَرَاءَهُمْ يَصْرُخُونَ وَيَصِيحُونَ وَهُمْ فِي بُكَاءٍ شَدِيدٍ زَائِدٍ
sentences.tr: wa-ahlu al-tājiri warāʾahum yaṣrukhūna wa-yaṣīḥūna wa-hum fī bukāʾin shadīdin zāʾidin
sentences.l: and the-family of-the-merchant behind-them, shrieking and-crying-out, and-they in weeping intense, excessive.
sentences.i: and the merchant's family behind them, shrieking and crying out in violent, unrestrained weeping.

sentences.t: فَأَوَّلُ مَنْ لَاقَى سَيِّدِي زَوْجَتُهُ وَأَوْلَادُهُ
sentences.tr: fa-awwalu man lāqā sayyidī zawjatuhu wa-awlāduhu
sentences.l: And-the-first who met my-master was his-wife and-his-children.
sentences.i: The first to meet my master were his wife and his children.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا رَآهُمْ بَهِتَ وَضَحِكَ وَثَبَتَ وَفَالَ لَهُمْ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā raʾāhum bahita wa-ḍaḥika wa-thabata wa-fāla lahum
sentences.l: And-when he-saw-them he-was-dumbfounded and-laughed and-steadied, and-said to-them:
sentences.i: When he saw them, he was dumbfounded, then laughed, then steadied himself, and said to them:
sentences.n: The print has وفال with fā for وقال, a compositor's slip; the letters are kept and the word is read “and he said”.

sentences.t: مَا حَالُكُمْ أَنْتُمْ وَمَا حَصَلَ لَكُمْ فِى الدَّارِ وَمَا جَرَى لَكُمْ
sentences.tr: mā ḥālukum antum wa-mā ḥaṣala lakum fī al-dāri wa-mā jarā lakum
sentences.l: What your-state, you, and-what befell to-you in the-house, and-what happened to-you?
sentences.i: How are you, and what has happened to you in the house? What has befallen you?

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا رَآوْهُ قَالُوا الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ عَلَى سَلَامَتِكَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā raʾawhu qālū al-ḥamdu li-Allāhi ʿalā salāmatika
sentences.l: And-when they-saw-him they-said: The-praise is-to-God for your-safety.
sentences.i: When they saw him they said: Praise God that you are safe.

sentences.t: وَرَمَوْا أَنْفُسَهُمْ عَلَيْهِ وَتَعَلَّقَتْ أَوْلَادُهُ بِهِ
sentences.tr: wa-ramaw anfusahum ʿalayhi wa-taʿallaqat awlāduhu bihi
sentences.l: and-they-threw themselves upon-him and-clung (f.) his-children to-him,
sentences.i: They threw themselves upon him, and his children clung to him,

sentences.t: وَصَاحُواوَا أَبَتَاهْ الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ عَلَى سَلَامَتِكَ يَا أَبَانَا
sentences.tr: wa-ṣāḥū wā-abatāh al-ḥamdu li-Allāhi ʿalā salāmatika yā abānā
sentences.l: and-they-cried-out: O my-father! The-praise is-to-God for your-safety, O our-father!
sentences.i: crying: Father! Praise God that you are safe, our father!
sentences.n: The print joins صاحوا and وا.

sentences.t: وَقَالَتْ لَهُ زَوْجَتُهُ أَنْتَ طَيِّبٌ الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي أَرَانَا وَجْهَكَ بِسَلَامَةٍ
sentences.tr: wa-qālat lahu zawjatuhu anta ṭayyibun al-ḥamdu li-Allāhi alladhī arānā wajhaka bi-salāmatin
sentences.l: and-said to-him his-wife: You are-well? The-praise is-to-God who showed-us your-face in safety.
sentences.i: and his wife said to him: Are you well? Praise God, who has shown us your face in safety.

sentences.t: وَقَدِ انْدَهَشَتْ وَطَارَ عَقْلُهَا لِمَارَأَتْهُ
sentences.tr: wa-qadi indahashat wa-ṭāra ʿaqluhā li-mā raʾathu
sentences.l: and-she-had been-bewildered and-flew her-mind at-what she-saw-him,
sentences.i: She was bewildered, and her wits had flown at the sight of him,
sentences.n: The print joins لما and راته (لما رأته).

sentences.t: وَقَالَتْ لَهُ يَا سَيِّدِى كَيْفَ كَانَتْ سَلَامَتُكَ أَنْتَ وَأَصْحَابُكَ التُّجَّارُ
sentences.tr: wa-qālat lahu yā sayyidī kayfa kānat salāmatuka anta wa-aṣḥābuka al-tujjāru
sentences.l: and-she-said to-him: O my-master, how was your-safety, you and-your-companions the-merchants?
sentences.i: and she said to him: My master, how have you fared, you and your merchant friends?

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهَا وَكَيْفَ كَانَ حَالُكُمْ فِى الدَّارِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahā wa-kayfa kāna ḥālukum fī al-dāri
sentences.l: So-he-said to-her: And-how was your-state in the-house?
sentences.i: He said to her: And how were you in the house?

sentences.t: فَقَالُوا نَحْنُ طَيِّبُونَ بِخَيْرٍ وَعَافِيَةٍ وَمَا أَصَابَ دَارَنَاشَيْ مِنَ الشَّرِّ
sentences.tr: fa-qālū naḥnu ṭayyibūna bi-khayrin wa-ʿāfiyatin wa-mā aṣāba dārana shay min al-sharri
sentences.l: So-they-said: We are-well, in goodness and-health, and-not struck our-house anything of the-evil,
sentences.i: They said: We are well, in good health, and no harm of any kind has touched our house,
sentences.n: The print joins دارنا and شي. Read as دارنا شيء, “anything (befell) our house”, with the hamza dropped as in speech (colloquial شي).

sentences.t: غَيْرَأَنَّ عَبْدَكَ كَافُورَ جَاءَ إِلَيْنَا وَهُوَ مَكْشُوفُ الرَّأْسِ مُخَرَّقُ الْأَثْوَابِ وَهُوَ يَصِيحُ وَاسَيِّدَاهْ وَاسَيِّدَاهْ
sentences.tr: ghayra anna ʿabdaka Kāfūra jāʾa ilaynā wa-huwa makshūfu al-raʾsi mukharraqu al-athwābi wa-huwa yaṣīḥu wā-sayyidāh wā-sayyidāh
sentences.l: except that your-slave Kāfūr came to-us, and-he bare-of-head, torn-of-garments, and-he crying: O my-master! O my-master!
sentences.i: except that your slave Kāfūr came to us bareheaded and with his clothes torn, crying: Oh, my master! Oh, my master!
sentences.n: The print joins غير and ان (غير أن); here it is read ghayra anna.

sentences.t: فَقُلْنَا لَهُ مَا الْخَبَرُ يَا كَافُورُ
sentences.tr: fa-qulnā lahu mā al-khabaru yā Kāfūru
sentences.l: So-we-said to-him: What the-news, O Kāfūr?
sentences.i: We said to him: What is the matter, Kāfūr?

sentences.t: فَقَالَ إِنَّ سَيِّدِي وَأَصْحَابَهُ التُّجَّارَ وَقَعَتْ عَلَيْهِمْ حَائِطٌ فِى الْبُسْتَانِ وَمَاتُوا جَمِيعًا
sentences.tr: fa-qāla inna sayyidī wa-aṣḥābahu al-tujjāra waqaʿat ʿalayhim ḥāʾiṭun fī al-bustāni wa-mātū jamīʿan
sentences.l: So-he-said: Indeed my-master and-his-companions the-merchants, fell upon-them a-wall in the-garden and-they-died, all.
sentences.i: He said: My master and his merchant friends — a wall in the garden fell on them, and they all died.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُمْ وَاللَّهِ إِنَّهُ أَتَانِي فِي هَذِهِ السَّاعَةِ وَهُوَ يَصِيحُ وَاسِتَّاهْ وَاوْلَادِسِتَّاهْ وَقَالَ إِنَّ سَيِّدَتِي وَأَوْلَادَهَا مَاتُوا جَمِيعًا
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahum wa-Allāhi innahu atānī fī hādhihi al-sāʿati wa-huwa yaṣīḥu wā-sittāh wā-wlādisittāh wa-qāla inna sayyidatī wa-awlādahā mātū jamīʿan
sentences.l: So-he-said to-them: By-God, indeed-he came-to-me at this the-hour, and-he crying: O my-lady! O the-children-of-my-lady! and-he-said: Indeed my-mistress and-her-children died, all.
sentences.i: He said to them: By God, he came to me just now crying: Oh, my lady! Oh, my lady's children! and he said that my mistress and her children had all died.
sentences.n: واولادستاه is run together in the print: wā + wlād (colloquial “children”) + sittāh; read here as one cry.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ نَظَرَ إِلَى جَانِبِهِ فَرَآنِي وَعِمَا مَتِي مَخْرُوقَةٌ فِي رَأْسِي
sentences.tr: thumma naẓara ilā jānibihi fa-raʾānī wa-ʿimā matī makhrūqatun fī raʾsī
sentences.l: Then he-looked to his-side and-saw-me, and-my-turban torn on my-head,
sentences.i: Then he glanced beside him and saw me, my turban torn on my head,
sentences.n: The print splits عمامتي as عما متي.

sentences.t: وَأَنَا أَصِيحُ وَأَبْكِي بُكَاءً شَدِيدًا وَأَحْثُوا التُّرَابَ عَلَى رَأْسِي
sentences.tr: wa-anā aṣīḥu wa-abkī bukāʾan shadīdan wa-aḥthū al-turāba ʿalā raʾsī
sentences.l: and-I crying-out and-weeping an-intense weeping and-throwing the-dust on my-head.
sentences.i: crying out, weeping bitterly and throwing dust on my head.
sentences.n: أحثوا is spelled with a final alif after the wāw, which the print often adds to verb endings in -ū.

sentences.t: فَصَرَخَ عَلَيَّ فَأَقْبَلْتُ عَلَيْهِ
sentences.tr: fa-ṣarakha ʿalayya fa-aqbaltu ʿalayhi
sentences.l: So-he-shouted at-me, and-I-approached him.
sentences.i: He shouted at me, and I went up to him.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لِي وَيْلَكَ يَا عَبْدَ النَّحْسِ يَا ابْنَ الزَّانِيَةِ يَا مَلْعُونَ الْجِنْسِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lī waylaka yā ʿabda al-naḥsi yā ibna al-zāniyati yā malʿūna al-jinsi
sentences.l: So-he-said to-me: Woe-to-you, O slave of-ill-omen, O son of-the-fornicatress, O accursed of-stock!
sentences.i: He said to me: Woe to you, you slave of ill omen, you whore's son, you accursed breed!

sentences.t: مَا هَذِهِ الْوَقَٰئِعُ الَّتِي عَمِلْتَهَا
sentences.tr: mā hādhihi al-waqāʾiʿu allatī ʿamiltahā
sentences.l: What are-these the-events which you-did?
sentences.i: What are these doings that you have done?
sentences.n: الوقئع is a defective spelling of الوقائع, “events, doings”.

sentences.t: وَلَكِنْ وَاللَّهِ لَأَ سْلُخَنَّ جِلْدَكَ مِنْ لَحْمِكَ وَأَقْطَعَنَّ لَحْمَكَ مِنْ عَظْمِكَ
sentences.tr: wa-lākin wa-Allāhi la-a-slukhanna jildaka min laḥmika wa-aqṭaʿanna laḥmaka min ʿaẓmika
sentences.l: But by-God, I-will-surely-flay your-skin from your-flesh and-I-will-surely-cut your-flesh from your-bone!
sentences.i: But by God, I will skin you from your flesh and cut your flesh from your bone!
sentences.n: The print splits the oath-verb as لا سلخن; واقطعن lacks the oath lām (expected ولأقطعن). Both are read as emphatic futures with nūn of emphasis.

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ لَهُ وَاللَّهِ مَا تَقْدِرُ تَعْمَلُ مَعِي شَيْئًا لِأَنَّكَ قَدِ اشْتَرَيْتَنِي عَلَى عَيْبِي بِهَذَا الشَّرْطِ
sentences.tr: fa-qultu lahu wa-Allāhi mā taqdiru taʿmalu maʿī shayʾan li-annaka qadi ishtaraytanī ʿalā ʿaybī bi-hādhā al-sharṭi
sentences.l: So-I-said to-him: By-God, you-cannot do with-me anything, because-you have bought-me with my-defect on this the-condition,
sentences.i: I said to him: By God, you can do nothing to me, because you bought me with my defect, on this condition,
sentences.n: Again taqdiru taʿmalu stands without أن, as in colloquial speech.

sentences.t: وَالشُّهُودُ يَشْهَدُونَ عَلَيْكَ حِينَ اشْتَرَيْتَنِي عَلَى عَيْبِي وَأَنْتَ عَالِمٌ بِهِ
sentences.tr: wa-al-shuhūdu yashhadūna ʿalayka ḥīna ishtaraytanī ʿalā ʿaybī wa-anta ʿālimun bihi
sentences.l: and the-witnesses bear-witness against-you, when you-bought-me with my-defect, and-you knowing of-it,
sentences.i: and the witnesses bear witness against you that you bought me with my defect and knew of it,

sentences.t: وَهُوَ أَنِّي أَكْذِبُ فِي كُلِّ سَنَةٍ كَذْبَةً وَاحِدَةً
sentences.tr: wa-huwa annī akdhibu fī kulli sanatin kadhbatan wāḥidatan
sentences.l: and it is that-I lie in every year one-lie, a single one.
sentences.i: namely, that I tell one lie in every year.

sentences.t: وَهَذِهِ نِصْفُ كَذْبَةٍ
sentences.tr: wa-hādhihi niṣfu kadhbatin
sentences.l: And this is half of-a-lie.
sentences.i: And this is half a lie.

sentences.t: فَإِذَا كَمُلَتِ السَّنَةُ كَذَبْتُ نِصْفَهَا الْآخَرَ فَتَبْقَى كَذْبَةٌ كَامِلَةٌ
sentences.tr: fa-idhā kamulati al-sanatu kadhabtu niṣfahā al-ākhara fa-tabqā kadhbatun kāmilatun
sentences.l: So-when the-year is-completed, I-will-lie its-half the-other, and-there-remains a-lie complete.
sentences.i: When the year is complete I will tell the other half of it, and that will leave one whole lie.

sentences.t: فَصَاحَ عَلَيَّ يَا كَلْبُ بْنَ الْكَلْبِ يَا أَلْعَنَ الْعَبِيدِ
sentences.tr: fa-ṣāḥa ʿalayya yā kalbu bna al-kalbi yā alʿana al-ʿabīdi
sentences.l: So-he-shouted at-me: O dog, son of-the-dog! O most-accursed of-slaves!
sentences.i: He shouted at me: You dog, son of a dog! You most cursed of slaves!

sentences.t: هَلْ هَذِهِ كُلُّهَا نِصْفُ كَذْبَةٍ وَإِنَّمَا هِيَ دَاهِيَةٌ كَبِيرَةٌ
sentences.tr: hal hādhihi kulluhā niṣfu kadhbatin wa-innamā hiya dāhiyatun kabīratun
sentences.l: Is this, all-of-it, half of-a-lie? Rather it is a-calamity, great.
sentences.i: Is all this half a lie? It is a great calamity!

sentences.t: اذْهَبْ عَنِّي فَأَنْتَ حُرٌّ لِوَجْهِ اللَّهِ
sentences.tr: idhhab ʿannī fa-anta ḥurrun li-wajhi Allāhi
sentences.l: Go from-me, for you are free for the-face of-God.
sentences.i: Get away from me: you are free, for God's sake.
sentences.n: لوجه الله, “for the face of God”, is the formula for doing something for God's sake alone, with no return.

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ وَاللَّهِ إِنْ أَعْتَقْتَنِي أَنْتَ مَا أُعْتِقُكَ أَنَا حَتَّى تَكْمُلَ السَّنَةُ وَأَكْذِبَ نِصْفَ الْكَذْبَةِ الْبَاقِيَةِ
sentences.tr: fa-qultu wa-Allāhi in aʿtaqtanī anta mā uʿtiquka anā ḥattā takmula al-sanatu wa-akdhiba niṣfa al-kadhbati al-bāqiyati
sentences.l: So-I-said: And-by-God, if you-freed-me, you, I-do-not-free-you, I, until the-year is-completed and-I-lie the-half of-the-lie, the-remaining,
sentences.i: So I said: By God, if you free me, I will not free you in return, not until the year is out and I have told the remaining half of the lie.
sentences.n: ما أُعْتِقُكَ أَنَا is Kāfūr's turn of phrase: you free me, I do not free you, that is, I do not release you from the bargain. The imperfect after ما is a plain present-future, and the pronoun أنا is stressed. حتى takes the subjunctive: تكمل … واكذب.

sentences.t: وَبَعْدَ أَنْ أُتِمَّهَا فَانْزِلْ بِي السُّوقَ وَبِعْنِي بِمَا اشْتَرَيْتَنِي بِهِ عَلَى عَيْبِي
sentences.tr: wa-baʿda an utimmahā fa-inzil bī al-sūqa wa-biʿnī bi-mā ishtaraytanī bihi ʿalā ʿaybī
sentences.l: And-after that I-complete-it, then-go-down with-me to-the-market, and-sell-me for-what you-bought-me with-it, upon my-flaw,
sentences.i: And once I have finished it, take me down to the market and sell me for what you paid for me, flaw and all.
sentences.n: فاء الجواب after the temporal clause: فَانْزِلْ is the main command. نزل بي is 'take me down'; على عيبي 'on my flaw' means 'with my flaw as it stands'.

sentences.t: وَلَا تُعْتِقْنِي لِأَنَّ مَا مَعِي صَنْعَةٌ أَقْتَاتُ مِنْهَا
sentences.tr: wa-lā tuʿtiqnī li-anna mā maʿī ṣanʿatun aqtātu minhā
sentences.l: And-do-not free-me, because not with-me is-a-craft I-live from-it.
sentences.i: And do not free me, for I have no trade to live by.

sentences.t: وَهَذِهِ الْمَسْئَلَةُ الَّتِي ذَكَرْتُهَالَكَ شَرْعِيَّةٌ ذَكَرَهَا الْفُقَهَاءُ فِي بَابِ الْعِتْقِ
sentences.tr: wa-hādhihi al-masʾalatu allatī dhakartuhā laka sharʿiyyatun dhakarahā al-fuqahāʾu fī bābi al-ʿitqi
sentences.l: And-this the-question which I-mentioned-it to-you is-legal; mentioned-it the-jurists in the-chapter of-the-manumission.
sentences.i: And this question that I have raised with you is a point of law: the jurists discuss it in the chapter on manumission.
sentences.n: The print joins ذكرتها لك into one word, ذكرتهالك, and spells المسئلة with yā-hamza; both kept as printed.

sentences.t: فَبَيْنَمَا نَحْنُ فِى الْكَلَامِ وَإِذَا بِالْخَلَائِقِ وَالنَّاسِ وَأَهْلِ الْحَارَةِ مِنْ نِسَاءٍ وَرِجَالٍ قَدْ جَاؤُا يَعْمَلُونَ الْعَزَاءَ
sentences.tr: fa-baynamā naḥnu fī al-kalāmi wa-idhā bi-al-khalāʾiqi wa-al-nāsi wa-ahli al-ḥārati min nisāʾin wa-rijālin qad jāʾū yaʿmalūna al-ʿazāʾa
sentences.l: And-while we in the-talk, and-behold the-crowds and-the-people and-folk of-the-quarter, of women and-men, had come, making the-mourning,
sentences.i: While we were still talking, behold, the crowds and the people and the folk of the quarter, women and men, had come to hold the mourning.
sentences.n: وإذا بـ: the bi- after إذا of surprise only marks what appears. يعملون العزاء 'make the mourning' is the idiom for holding a condolence gathering.

sentences.t: وَجَاءَ الْوَالِي وَجَمَا عَتُهُ فَرَاحَ سَيِّدِي وَالتُّجَّارُ إِلَى الْوَالِي وَأَعْلَمُوهُ بِالْقَضِيَّةِ وَأَنَّ هَذِهِ نِصْفُ كَذْبَةٍ
sentences.tr: wa-jāʾa al-wālī wa-jamā ʿatuhu fa-rāḥa sayyidī wa-al-tujjāru ilā al-wālī wa-aʿlamūhu bi-al-qaḍiyyati wa-anna hādhihi niṣfu kadhbatin
sentences.l: And-came the-governor and-his-company; so-went my-master and-the-merchants to the-governor and-informed-him of-the-case, and-that this is a-half of-a-lie.
sentences.i: The governor came with his men, and my master and the merchants went to the governor and told him the case, and that this was half a lie.
sentences.n: The print breaks جماعته in two (جما عته); kept as printed.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعُوا ذَلِكَ مِنْهُ اسْتَعْظَمُوا تِلْكَ الْكَذْبَةَ وَتَعَجَّبُوا غَايَةَ الْعَجَبِ فَلَعَنُونِي وَشَتَمُونِي
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿū dhālika minhu istaʿẓamū tilka al-kadhbata wa-taʿajjabū ghāyata al-ʿajabi fa-laʿanūnī wa-shatamūnī
sentences.l: And-when they-heard that from-him they-thought-great that lie and-marvelled the-utmost of-marvel, and-they-cursed-me and-reviled-me.
sentences.i: When they heard that from him, they thought it a monstrous lie, and marvelled beyond measure, and they cursed and reviled me.

sentences.t: فَبَقِيتُ وَاقِفًا أَضْحَكُ وَأَقُولُ كَيْفَ يَقْتُلُنِي سَيِّدِي وَقَدِ اشْتَرَانِي عَلَى هَذَا الْعَيْبِ
sentences.tr: fa-baqītu wāqifan aḍḥaku wa-aqūlu kayfa yaqtulunī sayyidī wa-qadi ishtarānī ʿalā hādhā al-ʿaybi
sentences.l: And-I-remained standing, I-laugh and-I-say: How would-he-kill-me, my-master, when-he-has bought-me upon this flaw?
sentences.i: I stood there laughing and saying: How can my master kill me, when he bought me with this very flaw?

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا مَضَى سَيِّدِي إِلَى الْبَيْتِ وَجَدَهُ خَرَابًا وَأَنَا الَّذِي أَخْرَبْتُ مُعْظَمَهُ وَأَكْثَرَهُ وَكَسَرْتُ فِيهِ شَيْئًا يُسَاوِي جُمْلَةً مِنَ الْمَالِ وَكَذَلِكَ زَوْجَتُهُ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā maḍā sayyidī ilā al-bayti wajadahu kharāban wa-anā alladhī akhrabtu muʿẓamahu wa-aktharahu wa-kasartu fīhi shayʾan yusāwī jumlatan min al-māli wa-kadhālika zawjatuhu
sentences.l: And-when went my-master to the-house he-found-it a-ruin, and-I am the-one-who ruined the-greater-part of-it and-the-most of-it, and-broke in-it a-thing worth a-sum of the-money, and-likewise his-wife.
sentences.i: When my master went home, he found it in ruins; I was the one who had wrecked most of it and the greater part of it, and broken things in it worth a good sum of money. And his wife found it likewise.
sentences.n: وكذلك زوجته is obscure in a text with no verb: it most likely means that his wife found it so too (or took him to see it); read with the next sentence, where she names Kāfūr.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ لَهُ زَوْجَتُهُ إِنَّ كَافُورًا هُوَالَّذِي كَسَرَ الْأَوَانِيَ وَالصِّينِيَّ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat lahu zawjatuhu inna Kāfūran huwa-alladhī kasara al-awānī wa-al-ṣīniyya
sentences.l: And-said to-him his-wife: Indeed Kāfūr, he-is-the-one-who broke the-vessels and-the-china.
sentences.i: His wife said to him: It was Kāfūr who smashed the vessels and the china.
sentences.n: The print joins هو الذي as هوالذي. الصيني is the Chinese-ware, porcelain.

sentences.t: فَازْدَادَ غَيْظُهُ وَضَرَبَ يَدًا عَلَى يَدٍ وَقَالَ وَاللَّهِ عُمْرِي مَا رَأَيْتُ وَلَدَ زِنًا مِثْلَ هَذَا الْعَبْدِ وَيَقُولُ إِنَّهَا نِصْفُ كَذْبَةٍ
sentences.tr: fa-izdāda ghayẓuhu wa-ḍaraba yadan ʿalā yadin wa-qāla wa-Allāhi ʿumrī mā raʾaytu walada zinan mithla hādhā al-ʿabdi wa-yaqūlu innahā niṣfu kadhbatin
sentences.l: And-increased his-rage, and-he-struck a-hand upon a-hand, and-said: By-God, my-life, I-have-not seen a-child of-fornication like this slave, and-he-says it is a-half of-a-lie!
sentences.i: His rage grew, and he struck palm on palm, and said: By God, in all my life I have never seen a bastard like this slave, who says that it was only half a lie!
sentences.n: ضرب يدا على يد (striking one hand on the other) shows anger or dismay. ولد زنا is 'child of fornication', the standard insult 'bastard'. عمري ما 'my life, I have not' is a common oath-like intensifier for 'never in my life'.

sentences.t: فَكَيْفَ لَوْ كَانَتْ كَذْبَةً كَامِلَةً كَانَ أَغْرَبَ مَدِينَةً أَوْ مَدِينَتَيْنِ
sentences.tr: fa-kayfa law kānat kadhbatan kāmilatan kāna aghraba madīnatan aw madīnatayni
sentences.l: And-how if it-were a-lie, whole: it-would-be he-estranged a-city or two-cities.
sentences.i: What if it were a whole lie? He would have ruined a city or two!
sentences.n: كان اغرب is printed so. The sense calls for اخرب 'he would have laid waste' (a city or two), and غ for خ looks like a compositor's slip; it is vocalised with the printed letters, as أَغْرَبَ, and translated by the evident sense. The missing لـ on the apodosis is usual in this register.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّهُ مِنْ شِدَّةِ غَيْظِهِ ذَهَبَ إِلَى الْوَالِي وَأَطْعَمَنِي عَلَقَةً نَظِيفَةً حَتَّى غِبْتُ عَنِ الدُّنْيَا وَغُشِيَ عَلَيَّ
sentences.tr: thumma innahu min shiddati ghayẓihi dhahaba ilā al-wālī wa-aṭʿamanī ʿalaqatan naẓīfatan ḥattā ghibtu ʿani al-dunyā wa-ghushiya ʿalayya
sentences.l: Then indeed-he, from the-intensity of-his-rage, went to the-governor, and-fed-me a-beating, clean, until I-was-absent from the-world and-it-was-swooned upon me.
sentences.i: Then, in the violence of his rage, he went to the governor, and had me given a thorough thrashing, until I was gone from the world and fainted away.
sentences.n: The subject of أطعمني is not stated: the master or the governor (who, as magistrate, orders it). علقة 'a beating' (lit. a leech-clot, a drubbing) with نظيفة 'clean' means a complete, thorough one. غشي علي is the impersonal passive 'it was swooned upon me', that is, I lost consciousness.

sentences.t: فَخَلَّانِي فِي غَشْيَتِي وَأَتَانِي بِالْمُزَيِّنِ فَخَصَانِي وَكَوَانِي فَمَا أَفَقْتُ إِلَّاوَجَدْتُ نَفْسِي طَوَاشِيًا
sentences.tr: fa-khallānī fī ghashyatī wa-atānī bi-al-muzayyini fa-khaṣānī wa-kawānī fa-mā afaqtu illā-wajadtu nafsī ṭawāshiyan
sentences.l: And-he-left-me in my-swoon, and-brought-me the-barber, and-he-castrated-me and-cauterised-me; and-I-did-not-come-to except-I-found myself a-eunuch.
sentences.i: He left me lying in my swoon and fetched the barber, who castrated me and cauterised the wound; and when I came to, I found myself a eunuch.
sentences.n: The print joins الا وجدت into one word. ما … إلا 'not … but' here means 'no sooner … than'. طواشي is the Turkish-derived word for a eunuch. أتاني بـ 'brought me' (lit. came to me with); the bi- is the verb's own preposition.

sentences.t: وَقَالَ لِي سَيِّدِي مِثْلَ مَا أَحْرَقْتَ قَلْبِي عَلَى أَعَزِّ الْأَشْيَاءِ عِنْدِي أَحْرَقْتُ قَلْبَكَ عَلَى أَعَزِّ الْأَعْضَاءِ عِنْدَكَ
sentences.tr: wa-qāla lī sayyidī mithla mā aḥraqta qalbī ʿalā aʿazzi al-ashyāʾi ʿindī aḥraqtu qalbaka ʿalā aʿazzi al-aʿḍāʾi ʿindaka
sentences.l: And-said to-me my-master: Like what you-burned my-heart over the-dearest of-things with me, I-burned your-heart over the-dearest of-limbs with you.
sentences.i: And my master said to me: As you burned my heart over the thing most dear to me, I have burned your heart over the limb most dear to you.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَخَذَنِي وَبَاعَنِي بِأَغْلَى ثَمَنٍ لِأَنِّي صِرْتُ طَوَاشِيًا
sentences.tr: thumma akhadhanī wa-bāʿanī bi-aghlā thamanin li-annī ṣirtu ṭawāshiyan
sentences.l: Then he-took-me and-sold-me for the-dearest price, because-I had-become a-eunuch.
sentences.i: Then he took me and sold me at the highest price, because I had become a eunuch.

sentences.t: وَمَا زِلْتُ أَلْقَى الْفِتَنَ فِى الْأَمَاكِنِ الَّتِي أُبَاعُ فِيهَا وَأَنْتَقِلُ مِنْ أَمِيرٍإِلَى أَمِيرٍ وَمِنْ كَبِيرٍ أَىِّ كَبِيرٍ أُبَاعُ وَأُشْرَى حَتَّى دَخَلْتُ قَصْرَ أَمِيرِالْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَقَدِ انْكَسَرَتْ نَفْسِي وَأَبَتْ حِيَلِي وَعَدِمْتُ خُصَايَ
sentences.tr: wa-mā ziltu alqā al-fitana fī al-amākini allatī ubāʿu fīhā wa-antaqilu min amīrin ilā amīrin wa-min kabīrin ayyi kabīrin ubāʿu wa-ushrā ḥattā dakhaltu qaṣra amīri al-muʾminīna wa-qadi inkasarat nafsī wa-abat ḥīlī wa-ʿadimtu khuṣāya
sentences.l: And-I-did-not cease I-meet the-troubles in the-places which I-am-sold in-them, and-I-move from an-emir to an-emir, and-from a-great-man to any great-man I-am-sold and-I-am-bought, until I-entered the-palace of-the-Commander of-the-Believers; and-had-broken my-spirit, and-refused my-devices, and-I-lacked my-testicles.
sentences.i: I never stopped meeting with trouble in the places where I was sold, passing from emir to emir and from one great man to another, sold and bought again, until I entered the palace of the Commander of the Faithful. By then my spirit was broken, my wits had failed, and I had lost my testicles.
sentences.n: In the print, أميرالى and أميرالمؤمنين are written as single words. اي كبير is printed so; it may be a dropped lām for الى كبير ('to a great man'), but 'any great man' also reads. أُباع وأُشرى are printed with a damma on the alif, kept. خصاي is Middle Arabic for خُصْيَيَّ 'my testicles'. The Arabic is blunt here, and so is the English.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ الْعَبْدَانِ كَلَامَهُ ضَحِكَا عَلَيْهِ وَقَالَا لَهُ إِنَّكَ خُرْوٌ ابْنُ خُرْءٍ تَكْذِبُ كَذِبًا شَنِيعًا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa al-ʿabdāni kalāmahu ḍaḥikā ʿalayhi wa-qālā lahu innaka khurwun ibnu khurʾin takdhibu kadhiban shanīʿan
sentences.l: And-when heard the-two-slaves his-speech they-laughed at-him and-said to-him: Indeed-you are dung, son of-dung; you-lie a-lie, hideous.
sentences.i: When the two slaves heard his story, they laughed at him and said: You are dung, the son of dung, and you tell a hideous lie!
sentences.n: خرو is a Middle Arabic spelling of خُرْء 'dung', with wāw for the hamza; the second word keeps the classical hamza spelling. ضحك على 'laugh at'.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قَالُوا لِلْعَبْدِ الثَّالِثِ اِحْكِ لَنَا حِكَايَتَكَ
sentences.tr: thumma qālū li-al-ʿabdi al-thālithi iḥki lanā ḥikāyataka
sentences.l: Then they-said to-the-slave, the-third: Tell for-us your-tale.
sentences.i: Then they said to the third slave: Tell us your story.

sentences.t: قَالَ لَهُمْ يَا أَوْلَادَ عَمِّي كُلَّمَا قُلْتُمُوهُ بَطَّالٌ فَأَنَا أَحْكِي لَكُمْ عَلَى سَبَبِ قَطْعِ خُصَايَ وَقَدْ كُنْتُ أَسْتَاهِلُ أَكْثَرَ مِنْ ذَلِكَ لِأَنِّي كُنْتُ نِكْتُ سِتِّي وَابْنَ سَيِّدِي
sentences.tr: qāla lahum yā awlāda ʿammī kullamā qultumūhu baṭṭālun fa-anā aḥkī lakum ʿalā sababi qaṭʿi khuṣāya wa-qad kuntu astāhilu akthara min dhālika li-annī kuntu niktu sittī wa-ibna sayyidī
sentences.l: He-said to-them: O sons of-my-paternal-uncle, all-that you-said is idle-talk; so-I will-tell to-you about the-cause of-the-cutting of-my-two-testicles. And-indeed I-was deserving more than that, because I-was (one-who) had-fucked my-lady and-the-son of-my-master.
sentences.i: He said to them: Cousins, everything you have said is idle talk. I will tell you how I came to be cut, and I deserved worse than that, because I had fucked my mistress and my master's son.
sentences.n: أبناء العم, “sons of the paternal uncle”, is a way of addressing fellow men as kin; the slaves are not literally cousins. كلما here means “all that, whatever”, and بطّال is read as “idle, worthless”. ستي is the contracted my-lady (sayyidatī); خصاي is a Middle Arabic dual-looking plural, “my testicles”; استاهل is the colloquial verb “deserve”. The sense of the opening is that their talk so far is mere chatter beside what he could tell.

sentences.t: وَالْحِكَايَةُ مَعِي طَوِيلَةٌ وَمَا هَذَا وَقْتُ حِكَايَتِهَا لِأَنَّ الصَّبَاحَ يَا أَوْلَادَ عَمِّي قَرِيبٌ وَرُبَّمَا يَطْلُعُ عَلَيْنَا الصَّبَاحُ وَمَعَنَا هَذَا الصُّنْدُوقُ فَنَبْقَى مَفْضُوحِينَ وَتَرُوحَ أَرْوَاحُنَا
sentences.tr: wa-al-ḥikāyatu maʿī ṭawīlatun wa-mā hādhā waqtu ḥikāyatihā li-anna al-ṣabāḥa yā awlāda ʿammī qarībun wa-rubbamā yaṭluʿu ʿalaynā al-ṣabāḥu wa-maʿanā hādhā al-ṣundūqu fa-nabqā mafḍūḥīna wa-tarūḥa arwāḥunā
sentences.l: And-the-tale with-me is long, and-this is not the-time of-its-telling, because the-morning, O sons of-my-paternal-uncle, is near; and-perhaps will-rise upon-us the-morning while-with-us is this chest, so-we-remain exposed-ones and-go (are-lost) our-souls.
sentences.i: My story is a long one, and this is no time to tell it, for the morning is near, cousins. If the dawn should rise on us with this chest still beside us, we would be exposed and our lives would be lost.
sentences.n: تروح ارواحنا: راح is the colloquial “go”, so “our souls go” means “we lose our lives”. The verb is pointed as a subjunctive to run on from فنبقى.

sentences.t: فَدُونَكُمْ فَتْحَ الْبَابِ فَإِذَا فَتَحْنَاهُ وَرُحْنَا إِلَى قَصْرِنَا قُلْتُ لَكُمْ عَلَى سَبَبِ قَطْعِ خُصَايَ
sentences.tr: fa-dūnakum fatḥa al-bābi fa-idhā fataḥnāhu wa-ruḥnā ilā qaṣrinā qultu lakum ʿalā sababi qaṭʿi khuṣāya
sentences.l: So-here-you-have (take) the-opening of-the-door; and-when we-have-opened-it and-gone to our-palace, I-have-told you about the-cause of-the-cutting of-my-testicles.
sentences.i: So get on with opening the door. When we have opened it and gone back to our palace, I will tell you how I came to be cut.
sentences.n: دونكم, “(here) before you”, is an urging to take something in hand. The perfect قلت لكم stands for a future promise after إذا, “I shall have told you”.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ تَعَلَّقَ وَنَزَلَ مِنَ الْحَائِطِ وَفَتَحَ الْبَابَ فَدَخَلُوا وَحَطُّوا الشَّمْعَ وَحَفَرُوا حُفْرَةً بِطُولِ الصُّنْدُوقِ وَعَرْضِهِ بَيْنَ أَرْبَعَةِ قُبُورٍ
sentences.tr: thumma taʿallaqa wa-nazala mina al-ḥāʾiṭi wa-fataḥa al-bāba fa-dakhalū wa-ḥaṭṭū al-shamʿa wa-ḥafarū ḥufratan bi-ṭūli al-ṣundūqi wa-ʿarḍihi bayna arbaʿati qubūrin
sentences.l: Then he-hung (by his hands) and-came-down from the-wall and-opened the-door, and-they-entered and-set-down the-candles and-dug a-hole at-the-length of-the-chest and-its-width between four tombs.
sentences.i: Then he hung from the top of the wall, dropped down, and opened the door, and they went in, set down the candles, and dug a pit the length and width of the chest, among four graves.
sentences.n: The subject of تعلق is not named; it is the slave who has just been speaking, who has to climb over the wall because the door is locked from inside.

sentences.t: وَصَارَ كَافُورُ يَحْفِرُ وَصَوَابُ يَنْقُلُ التُّرَابَ بِالْقُفَفِ إِلَى أَنْ حَفَرُوا نِصْفَ قَامَةٍ
sentences.tr: wa-ṣāra Kāfūru yaḥfiru wa-Ṣawābu yanqulu al-turāba bi-al-qufafi ilā an ḥafarū niṣfa qāmatin
sentences.l: And-became Kāfūr digging and-Ṣawāb carrying the-earth in-the-baskets until they-dug half a-stature.
sentences.i: Kāfūr dug while Ṣawāb carried the earth away in baskets, until they had dug down half a man's height.
sentences.n: Kāfūr and Ṣawāb are two of the slaves; Bukhayt is the first, who has already told his tale. After إلى أن the perfect حفروا is Middle Arabic for the classical subjunctive.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ حَطُّوا الصُّنْدُوقَ فِى الْحُفْرَةِ وَرَدُّوا عَلَيْهِ التُّرَابَ وَخَرَجُوا مِنَ التُّرْبَةِ وَرَدُّوا الْبَابَ وَغَابُوا عَنْ عَيْنِ غَانِمِ بْنِ أَيُّوبَ
sentences.tr: thumma ḥaṭṭū al-ṣundūqa fī al-ḥufrati wa-raddū ʿalayhi al-turāba wa-kharajū mina al-turbati wa-raddū al-bāba wa-ghābū ʿan ʿayni Ghānimi ibni Ayyūba
sentences.l: Then they-set-down the-chest in the-hole and-returned upon-it the-earth, and-went-out from the-graveyard and-shut the-door, and-were-absent from the-eye of Ghānim son of Ayyūb.
sentences.i: Then they lowered the chest into the pit, heaped the earth back over it, left the graveyard, shut the door behind them, and passed out of the sight of Ghānim ibn Ayyūb.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا اسْتَقَرَّ وَخَلَا لِغَانِمٍ الْمَكَانُ وَعَلِمَ أَنَّهُ وَحْدَهُ اشْتَغَلَ سِرُّهُ بِمَا فِى الصُّنْدُوقِ وَقَالَ فِي نَفْسِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā istaqarra wa-khalā li-Ghānimin al-makānu wa-ʿalima annahu waḥdahu ishtaghala sirruhu bi-mā fī al-ṣundūqi wa-qāla fī nafsihi
sentences.l: And-when it-settled and-was-empty for-Ghānim the-place, and-he-knew that-he was alone, his-inmost-mind became-busy with-what was in the-chest, and-he-said in his-self:
sentences.i: When everything had grown still and the place lay empty for Ghānim, and he knew he was alone, his mind became taken up with what was in the chest, and he said to himself:

sentences.t: يَا تَرَى أَيْشَ فِي هَذَا الصُّنْدُوقِ
sentences.tr: yā tarā aysha fī hādhā al-ṣundūqi
sentences.l: O one-sees (I wonder): what is in this chest?
sentences.i: I wonder what is in this chest.
sentences.n: يا ترى is a fixed phrase of wondering; ايش is the Middle Arabic contraction of أيّ شيء “what thing”.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ صَبَرَ حَتَّى بَرَقَ الْفَجْرُ وَلَاحَ وَبَانَ ضِيَاؤُهُ فَنَزَلَ مِنْ عَلَى النَّخْلَهِ وَأَزَالَ التُّرَابَ بِيَدِهِ حَتَّى كَشَفَ الصُّنْدُوقَ وَخَلَّصَهُ
sentences.tr: thumma ṣabara ḥattā baraqa al-fajru wa-lāḥa wa-bāna ḍiyāʾuhu fa-nazala min ʿalā al-nakhlahi wa-azāla al-turāba bi-yadihi ḥattā kashafa al-ṣundūqa wa-khallaṣahu
sentences.l: Then he-waited until flashed the-dawn and-shone, and-became-clear its-light; so-he-came-down from upon the-palm and-removed the-earth with-his-hand until he-uncovered the-chest and-freed-it.
sentences.i: Then he waited until the dawn flashed, broke, and its light grew clear. He came down from the palm tree, scraped the earth away with his hand until he had uncovered the chest, and freed it.
sentences.n: النخله: the print gives the final letter as ه, not ة; it is read as the ordinary nakhla “palm”. The hand-digging is done by Ghānim alone, with no spade.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَخَذَ حَجَرًا كَبِيرًا وَضَرَبَ بِهِ الْقُفْلَ فَكَسَرَهُ وَكَشَفَ الْغِطَاءَ
sentences.tr: thumma akhadha ḥajaran kabīran wa-ḍaraba bihi al-qufla fa-kasarahu wa-kashafa al-ghiṭāʾa
sentences.l: Then he-took a-stone, large, and-struck with-it the-lock, and-broke-it and-uncovered the-lid.
sentences.i: Then he took a large stone and struck the lock with it, and broke it and lifted the lid.

sentences.t: وَنَظَرَ فِيهِ فَإِذَا فِيهِ صَبِيَّةٌ نَائِمَةٌ مُبَنَّجَةٌ وَنَفَسُهَا طَالِعٌ نَازِلٌ إِلَّا أَنَّهَا ذَاتُ حُسْنٍ وَجَمَالٍ
sentences.tr: wa-naẓara fīhi fa-idhā fīhi ṣabiyyatun nāʾimatun mubannajatun wa-nafasuhā ṭāliʿun nāzilun illā annahā dhātu ḥusnin wa-jamālin
sentences.l: And-he-looked into-it, and-behold in-it was a-girl, sleeping, drugged, and-her-breath going-up and going-down; but that-she was possessor of-beauty and-comeliness.
sentences.i: He looked into it, and there lay a girl asleep, drugged, her breath rising and falling, but a woman of great beauty and grace.
sentences.n: The girl is called صبية “young girl” and later جارية “slave-girl”. مبنجة is “drugged with banj”, from the noun بنج “bang”, a knock-out drug.

sentences.t: وَعَلَيْهَا حُلِيٌّ وَمَصَاغُ ذَهَبٍ وَقِلَا بِدُ مِنَ الْجَوَاهِرِ تُسَاوِي مُلْكَ السُّلْطَانِ مَا يَفِي بِثَمَنِهَا مَالٌ
sentences.tr: wa-ʿalayhā ḥuliyyun wa-maṣāghu dhahabin wa-qilā bidu mina al-jawāhiri tusāwī mulka al-sulṭāni mā yafī bi-thamanihā mālun
sentences.l: And-upon-her were ornaments and-worked-things of-gold and-neck-laces of the-jewels, equalling the-kingdom of-the-sultan; no wealth suffices for-its-price.
sentences.i: She was wearing ornaments and gold jewellery and necklaces of precious stones, worth a sultan's whole kingdom; no sum of money could match their price.
sentences.n: قلا بد: the print splits the word. It is read as one word, قلابد, a plural of قلادة “necklace” (the usual plural is قلائد); the first part is pointed قِلَا and the second بِدُ. If the print is corrupt, the sense is still plainly jewellery.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا رَآهَا غَانِمُ بْنُ أَيُّوبَ عَرَفَ أَنَّهُمْ تَغَامَزُوا عَلَيْهَا وَبَنَّجُوهَا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā raʾāhā Ghānimu ibnu Ayyūba ʿarafa annahum taghāmazū ʿalayhā wa-bannajūhā
sentences.l: And-when saw-her Ghānim son of Ayyūb, he-knew that-they had-winked-together against-her and-drugged-her.
sentences.i: When Ghānim ibn Ayyūb saw her, he knew that they had plotted against her and drugged her.
sentences.n: تغامزوا عليها: “they winked at one another over her”, that is, conspired together to seize her.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا تَحَقَّقَ ذَلِكَ الْأَمْرَ عَالَجَ فِيهَا حَتَّى أَخْرَجَهَا مِنَ الصُّنْدُوقِ وَأَرْقَدَهَا عَلَى قَفَاهَا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā taḥaqqaqa dhālika al-amra ʿālaja fīhā ḥattā akhrajahā mina al-ṣundūqi wa-arqadahā ʿalā qafāhā
sentences.l: And-when he-made-sure (of) that, the-matter, he-laboured upon-her until he-brought-her-out from the-chest and-laid-her-down on her-nape (her back).
sentences.i: When he was sure of the matter, he worked at her until he had got her out of the chest and laid her on her back.
sentences.n: The print has تحقق governing a direct object (ذلك الأمر), where the classical idiom would use a preposition; the vowels follow the print.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا اسْتَنْشَقَتِ الْأَرْيَاحَ وَدَخَلَ الْهَوَاءُ فِي أَنْفِهَا وَمَنَافِسِهَا عَطَسَتْ ثُمَّ شَرِقَتْ وَسَعَلَتْ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā istanshaqat al-aryāḥa wa-dakhala al-hawāʾu fī anfihā wa-manāfisihā ʿaṭasat thumma shariqat wa-saʿalat
sentences.l: And-when she-breathed-in the-airs, and-entered the-air into her-nose and-her-breathing-places, she-sneezed, then choked, and-coughed.
sentences.i: When she drew in the breezes and the air entered her nose and nostrils, she sneezed, then choked and coughed.
sentences.n: منافسها: read as a plural of منفس “breathing-place”, that is, her air passages; the word is obscure and may be a slip for مناخرها “her nostrils”.

sentences.t: فَوَقَعَ مِنْ حَلْقِهَا قُرْصُ بَنْجٍ إِقْرِيطِشِيٍّ لَوْشَمَّهُ الْفِيلُ لَرَقَدَ مِنَ اللَّيْلِ إِلَى اللَّيْلِ
sentences.tr: fa-waqaʿa min ḥalqihā qurṣu banjin iqrīṭishiyyin lawshammahu al-fīlu la-raqada mina al-layli ilā al-layli
sentences.l: And-there-fell from her-throat a-disc of-bang, Cretan: had-smelled-it the-elephant, he-would-have-slept from night to night.
sentences.i: Out of her throat fell a pill of Cretan bang, so strong that an elephant who sniffed it would have slept from one night to the next.
sentences.n: Cretan bang (a narcotic) is the strongest kind in the stories; the pill had stuck in her throat. “From night to night” means a full day and night.

sentences.t: فَفَتَحَتْ عَيْنَيْهَا وَأَدَارَتْ طَرْفَهَا وَقَالَتْ بِكَلَامٍ عَذْبٍ فَصِيحٍ
sentences.tr: fa-fataḥat ʿaynayhā wa-adārat ṭarfahā wa-qālat bi-kalāmin ʿadhbin faṣīḥin
sentences.l: And-she-opened her-two-eyes and-turned her-glance, and-said in-speech, sweet, eloquent:
sentences.i: She opened her eyes, looked about, and said in sweet, fluent speech:

sentences.t: وَيْلَكِ يَارِيحُ مَا فِيكِ رِيٌّ لِلْعَطْشَانِ وَلَا أُنْسٌ لِلرَّيَّانِ أَيْنَ زَهْرُ الْبُسْتَانِ
sentences.tr: waylaki yā rīḥu mā fīki riyyun li-al-ʿaṭshāni wa-lā unsun li-al-rayyāni ayna zahru al-bustāni
sentences.l: Woe-to-you, O wind! There-is-not in-you quenching for-the-thirsty ‖ nor companionship for-the-sated ‖ where are the-blossoms of-the-garden?
sentences.i: Woe to you, wind! There is no drink in you for the thirsty and no company for the sated. Where are the flowers of the garden?
sentences.n: Rhymed prose (sajʿ) in -ān: al-ʿaṭshān, al-rayyān, al-bustān. Her words are unclear and may be a half-conscious address to the air she is breathing, or to her missing maidens (the “flowers of the garden”).

sentences.t: فَلَمْ يُجَاوِبْهَا أَحَدٌ فَالْتَفَتَتْ وَقَالَتْ يَاصَبِيحَةُ شَجَرَةَ الدُّرِّ نُورَ الْهُدَى نَجْمَةَ الصُّبْحِ أَنْتِ فِي شَهْرٍ نُزْهَةُ حُلْوَةُ ظَرِيفَةُ تَكَلَّمُوا
sentences.tr: fa-lam yujāwibhā aḥadun fa-iltafatat wa-qālat yā ṣabīḥatu shajarata al-durri nūra al-hudā najmata al-ṣubḥi anti fī shahrin nuzhatu ḥulwatu ẓarīfatu takallamū
sentences.l: And-not answered-her anyone; so-she-turned and-said: O Ṣabīḥa, Tree of Pearls, Light of Guidance, Star of-the-Morning, you in a-month, Nuzha, Ḥulwa, Ẓarīfa, speak!
sentences.i: No one answered her, so she turned and said: Ṣabīḥa, Shajarat al-Durr, Nūr al-Hudā, Najmat al-Ṣubḥ, Nuzha, Ḥulwa, Ẓarīfa, speak!
sentences.n: These look like the names of her waiting-women (Ṣabīḥa, Shajarat al-Durr, Nūr al-Hudā, Najmat al-Ṣubḥ, Nuzha, Ḥulwa, Ẓarīfa). The words أنت في شهر between two of them make no clear sense; they are pointed as printed and translated word for word, and may be a corruption of one or more further names.

sentences.t: فَلَمْ يُجِبْهَا أَحَدٌ فَجَالَتْ بِطَرْفِهَا فَقَالَتْ وَيْلِي تَقْبِرِينِي فِى الْقُبُورِ
sentences.tr: fa-lam yujibhā aḥadun fa-jālat bi-ṭarfihā fa-qālat waylī taqbirīnī fī al-qubūri
sentences.l: And-not answered-her anyone; so-she-roved with-her-glance and-said: My-woe! You-bury-me among the-tombs.
sentences.i: Again no one answered her. She looked around and said: Woe is me! You are burying me among the graves!
sentences.n: تقبريني is pointed as a feminine singular address “you bury me”; whom she means is unclear, and the form may be a slip for the plural تقبروني.

sentences.t: يَا مَنْ يَعْلَمُ مَافِى الصُّدُورِ وَيُجَازِي يَوْمَ الْبَعْثِ وَالنُّشُورِ مَنْ جَاءَ بِي مِنْ بَيْنِ السُّتُورِ وَالْخُدُورِ وَضَعَنِي بَيْنَ أَرْبَعَةِ قُبُورٍ
sentences.tr: yā man yaʿlamu mā fī al-ṣudūri wa-yujāzī yawma al-baʿthi wa-al-nushūri man jāʾa bī min bayni al-sutūri wa-al-khudūri waḍaʿanī bayna arbaʿati qubūrin
sentences.l: O he-who knows what is in the-breasts ‖ and-repays on-the-day of-the-resurrection and-the-rising ‖ who came with-me from between the-curtains and-the-bowers ‖ and set-me between four tombs?
sentences.i: O You who know what lies in the breasts and repay on the Day of Resurrection and Rising: who brought me out from among curtains and women's bowers and set me down between four graves?
sentences.n: Rhymed prose (sajʿ) in -ūr: al-ṣudūr, al-nushūr, al-khudūr, qubūr. I take من جاء بي… as a question (“who brought me…?”), with وضعني following without a conjunction; it could also be read as God being addressed as the one who brought her. الخدور are the women's chambers or screened litters.

sentences.t: هَذَا كُلُّهُ وَغَانِمٌ وَاقِفٌ عَلَى حَيْلِهِ
sentences.tr: hādhā kulluhu wa-Ghānimun wāqifun ʿalā ḥaylihi
sentences.l: All-of-this, and-Ghānim standing upon his-strength.
sentences.i: All this while Ghānim stood where he was, steady on his feet.
sentences.n: على حيله: ḥayl is “strength, power”; the phrase is read as “on his own feet, without moving”. The sense is slightly uncertain.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهَا يَا سِتِّي لَاخُدُورَ وَلَا قُصُورَ وَلَا قُبُورَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahā yā sittī lā khudūra wa-lā quṣūra wa-lā qubūra
sentences.l: And-he-said to-her: O my-lady, no bowers ‖ and-no palaces ‖ and-no tombs —
sentences.i: He said to her: My lady, there are no bowers, no palaces, no graves,
sentences.n: Sajʿ continues in -ūr. The print runs لا and خدور together as one word.

sentences.t: مَا هُنَا إِلَّا عَبْدُكِ الْمَسْلُوبُ غَانِمُ بْنُ أَيُّوبَ وَقَدْ سَاقَهُ لَكِ عَلَّامُ الْغُيُوبِ حَتَّى يُنَجِّيَكِ مِنْ هَذِهِ الْكُرُوبِ وَيُحَصِّلَ لَكِ غَايَةَ الْمَطْلُوبِ وَسَكَتَ
sentences.tr: mā hunā illā ʿabduki al-maslūbu Ghānimu ibnu Ayyūba wa-qad sāqahu laki ʿallāmu al-ghuyūbi ḥattā yunajjiyaki min hādhihi al-kurūbi wa-yuḥaṣṣila laki ghāyata al-maṭlūbi wa-sakata
sentences.l: not here is but your-slave, the-despoiled, Ghānim son of Ayyūb ‖ and-indeed drove-him to-you the-Knower of-the-unseen-things ‖ so-that he-may-deliver-you from these distresses ‖ and-bring-about for-you the-furthest-end of-the-sought. ‖ And-he-fell-silent.
sentences.i: only your servant here, poor despoiled Ghānim ibn Ayyūb, whom the Knower of Hidden Things has driven to you, to deliver you from these troubles and bring you to the end of your desire. And he fell silent.
sentences.n: Sajʿ in -ūb: Ayyūb, al-ghuyūb, al-kurūb, al-maṭlūb. المسلوب “stripped, despoiled” is a self-deprecating epithet: a poor stripped fellow. The subject of يحصّل is God, as with ينجّيك.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا تَحَقَّقَتِ الْأَمْرَ قَالَتْ أَشْهَدُ أَنْ لَا آلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَأَشْهَدُ أَنَّ مُحَمَّدًا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā taḥaqqaqati al-amra qālat ashhadu an lā ilāha illā Allāhu wa-ashhadu anna Muḥammadan rasūlu Allāhi
sentences.l: And-when she-made-sure (of) the-matter, she-said: I-bear-witness that no god but God, and-I-bear-witness that Muḥammad is the-messenger of God.
sentences.i: When she understood how things stood, she said: I bear witness that there is no god but God, and I bear witness that Muḥammad is the messenger of God.
sentences.n: This is the Muslim profession of faith (shahāda). By saying it she shows herself a Muslim, so that Ghānim need not fear she is unclean or hostile. The print spells إله with a madda, آله.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ الْتَفَتَتْ إِلَى غَانِمٍ وَقَدْ وَضَعَتْ يَدَيْهَا عَلَى وَجْهِهَا وَقَالَتْ لَهُ بِكَلَامٍ عَذْبٍ
sentences.tr: thumma iltafatat ilā Ghānimin wa-qad waḍaʿat yadayhā ʿalā wajhihā wa-qālat lahu bi-kalāmin ʿadhbin
sentences.l: Then she-turned to Ghānim, having put her-two-hands upon her-face, and-said to-him in-speech, sweet:
sentences.i: Then she turned to Ghānim, covering her face with her hands, and said to him in her sweet voice:

sentences.t: أَيُّهَا الشَّابُّ الْمُبَارَكُ مَنْ جَاءَ بِي إِلَى هَذَا الْمَكَانِ فَهَا أَنَا قَدَا فَقْتُ
sentences.tr: ayyuhā al-shābbu al-mubāraku man jāʾa bī ilā hādhā al-makāni fa-hā anā qad afaqtu
sentences.l: O young-man, the-blessed: who brought me to this place? For-here I, already I-have-woken.
sentences.i: Blessed young man, who brought me to this place? For here I am, and I have come to myself.
sentences.n: قدا فقت: the print runs the alif of أفقت onto قد; read قد أفقت, “I have come to”. The two pieces are pointed separately as printed.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ يَاسِتِّي ثَلَٰثَةُ عَبِيدٍ خَصِيُّونَ أَتَوْا وَهُمْ حَامِلُونَ هَذَا الصُّنْدُوقَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla yā sittī thalāthatu ʿabīdin khaṣiyyūna ataw wa-hum ḥāmilūna hādhā al-ṣundūqa
sentences.l: And-he-said: O my-lady, three slaves, eunuchs, came, and-they carrying this chest.
sentences.i: He said: My lady, three slave eunuchs came here carrying this chest.
sentences.n: The print has ثلثة without the long ā of ثلاثة; a dagger alif is supplied. The print runs يا and ستي together.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ حَكَى لَهَا جَمِيعَ مَا جَرَى لَهُ وَكَيْفَ أَمْسَى عَلَيْهِ لْمَسَاءُ حَتَّى كَانَ سَبَبَ سَلَامَتِهَا وَإِلَّا كَانَتْ مَاتَتْ بِغُصَّتِهَا
sentences.tr: thumma ḥakā lahā jamīʿa mā jarā lahu wa-kayfa amsā ʿalayhi al-masāʾu ḥattā kāna sababa salāmatihā wa-illā kānat mātat bi-ghuṣṣatihā
sentences.l: Then he-related to-her all-of what happened to-him, and-how the-evening came-upon him, until he-became the-cause of-her-safety — and-otherwise she-would-have died of-her-choking.
sentences.i: Then he told her everything that had happened to him, and how evening had overtaken him, so that he became the cause of her rescue; otherwise she would have died of her choking.
sentences.n: لمساء: the print loses the alif of the article, for المساء “the evening”. It is pointed as printed. غصّة is the choking of a morsel stuck in the throat, here the bang pill.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّهُ أَسْأَلَهَا عَنْ حِكَايَتِهَا وَخَبَرِهَا
sentences.tr: thumma innahu asʾalahā ʿan ḥikāyatihā wa-khabarihā
sentences.l: Then indeed-he asked-her about her-tale and-her-news.
sentences.i: Then he asked her about her story and her circumstances.
sentences.n: اسالها: read as سألها “he asked her”. The extra initial alif may be a slip or a Middle Arabic fourth-form look-alike, so it is pointed as the print has it.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ لَهُ أَيُّهَا الشَّابُّ الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي رَمَانِي عِنْدَ مِثْلِكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat lahu ayyuhā al-shābbu al-ḥamdu li-Allāhi alladhī ramānī ʿinda mithlika
sentences.l: And-she-said to-him: O young-man, the-praise is to-God who cast-me with the-like-of-you.
sentences.i: She said to him: Young man, praise be to God, who has cast me down beside one like you.

sentences.t: فَقُمِ الْآنَ وَحُطَّنِي فِى الصُّنْدُوقِ وَاخْرُجْ إِلَى الطَّرِيقِ
sentences.tr: fa-qumi al-āna wa-ḥuṭṭanī fī al-ṣundūqi wa-ukhruj ilā al-ṭarīqi
sentences.l: So-stand now, and-put-me in the-chest, and-go-out to the-road.
sentences.i: So get up now, put me back in the chest, and go out to the road.

sentences.t: فَإِذَا وَبَدْتَ مُكَارِيًا أَوْ بَغَّالًا فَاكْتَرِهِ لِحَمْلِ هَذَا الصُّنْدُوقِ وَوَصِّلْنِي إِلَى بَيْتِكَ
sentences.tr: fa-idhā wa-badta mukāriyan aw baghghālan fa-ikrihi li-ḥamli hādhā al-ṣundūqi wa-waṣṣilnī ilā baytika
sentences.l: And-when you-find a-muleteer or a-mule-driver, hire-him for-the-carrying of-this chest, and-have-me-delivered to your-house.
sentences.i: If you find a muleteer or a mule-driver, hire him to carry this chest, and have me taken to your house.
sentences.n: وبدت: the print gives ب where the sense needs ج, وجدت “you found”; it is pointed as printed. The ب-for-ج slip is a compositor's error.

sentences.t: فَذَا بَقِيتُ أَنَافِي دَارِكَ يَكُونُ خَيْرًا وَأَحْكِي لَكَ حِكَايَتِي وَأُخْبِرُكَ بِقِصَّتِي وَيَحْصُلُ لَكَ الْخَيْرُ مِنْ جِهَتِي
sentences.tr: fa-dhā baqītu anā fī dārika yakūnu khayran wa-aḥkī laka ḥikāyatī wa-ukhbiruka bi-qiṣṣatī wa-yaḥṣulu laka al-khayru min jihatī
sentences.l: So-if I-remain, I, in your-house it-will-be good, and-I-will-tell to-you my-tale and-inform-you of-my-story, and-there-will-accrue to-you the-good from my-side.
sentences.i: If I stay in your house, it will turn out well. I will tell you my story and recount my history, and good will come to you through me.
sentences.n: فذا is a slip for فإذا with the alif lost; انافي runs أنا and في together. The print again has a short noun clause with no إن or فـ-apodosis marker for the result, “it will be good”.

sentences.t: فَفَرِحَ وَخَرَجَ إِلَى ظَاهِرِ التُّرْبَةِ وَقَدْ شَعْشَعَ النَّهَارُ وَلَاحَ الْجَوُّ بِالْأَنْوَارِ وَخَرَجَتِ النَّاسُ وَمَشَوْا
sentences.tr: fa-fariḥa wa-kharaja ilā ẓāhiri al-turbati wa-qad shaʿshaʿa al-nahāru wa-lāḥa al-jawwu bi-al-anwāri wa-kharajati al-nāsu wa-mashaw
sentences.l: And-he-rejoiced and-went-out to the-outside of-the-graveyard, the-day having-spread-its-light, and-the-air shone with-lights, and-the-people went-out and-walked-about.
sentences.i: He was glad, and went out to the edge of the graveyard. The day had broadened into light and the air shone brightly, and the people were out and walking about.
sentences.n: The feminine verb خرجت with الناس and the plural ومشوا is a freedom the print allows itself.

sentences.t: فَاكْتَرَى رَجُلًا بِبَغْلٍ وَأَتَى بِهِ إِلَى التُّرْبَةِ وَشَالَ الصُّنْدُوقَ بَعْدَ مَا حَطَّ فِيهِ الصَّبِيَّةَ
sentences.tr: fa-iktarā rajulan bi-baghlin wa-atā bihi ilā al-turbati wa-shāla al-ṣundūqa baʿda mā ḥaṭṭa fīhi al-ṣabiyyata
sentences.l: And-he-hired a-man with-a-mule and-brought him to the-graveyard, and-he-lifted the-chest after that-he-put in-it the-girl.
sentences.i: He hired a man with a mule and brought him to the graveyard, and the man loaded up the chest after Ghānim had put the girl back in it.
sentences.n: شال is the colloquial “lift, carry up”. Grammatically the subject of شال could also be Ghānim, but the muleteer is the one hired for it.

sentences.t: وَوَقَعَتْ مَحَبَّتُهَا فِي قَلْبِهِ وَسَارَبِهَا وَهُوَ فَرْحَانُ لِأَنَّهَا جَارِيَةٌ تُسَاوِي عَشَرَةَ آلَافِ دِينَارٍ وَعَلَيْهَا حُلِيٌّ وَحُلَلٌ تُسَاوِي مَا لًا جَزِيلًا
sentences.tr: wa-waqaʿat maḥabbatuhā fī qalbihi wa-sāra bihā wa-huwa farḥānu li-annahā jāriyatun tusāwī ʿasharata ālāfi dīnārin wa-ʿalayhā ḥuliyyun wa-ḥulalun tusāwī mālan jazīlan
sentences.l: And-fell the-love-of-her in his-heart, and-he-went with-her, he rejoicing, because-she was a-girl worth ten thousands of-dinars, and-upon-her were ornaments and-robes worth wealth, abundant.
sentences.i: Love of her fell into his heart, and he set off with her, glad, because she was a slave-girl worth ten thousand dinars, and the jewels and robes she wore were worth a great fortune besides.
sentences.n: The print splits مالا “wealth” into ما لا; it is read as one word.

sentences.t: وَمَا صَدَّقَ أَنَّهُ يَصِلُ إِلَى دَارِهِ وَأَنْزَلَ الصُّنْدُوقَ وَفَتَحَهُ
sentences.tr: wa-mā ṣaddaqa annahu yaṣilu ilā dārihi wa-anzala al-ṣundūqa wa-fataḥahu
sentences.l: And-he-did-not believe that-he would-arrive at his-house, and-he-brought-down the-chest and-opened-it.
sentences.i: He could scarcely believe he would reach his house, and when he got there he unloaded the chest and opened it.
sentences.n: ما صدّق أنه يصل: “he hardly believed he would arrive”, the colloquial idiom for being impatient or relieved to arrive. The print marks the shadda on صدّق itself.

sentences.t: وَأَدْرَكَ شَهْرَزَادَ الصَّبَاحُ فَسَكَتَتْ عَنِ الْكَلَامِ الْمُبَاحِ
sentences.tr: wa-adraka Shahrazāda al-ṣabāḥu fa-sakatat ʿani al-kalāmi al-mubāḥi
sentences.l: And-overtook Shahrazād the-morning, and-she-fell-silent from the-speech, the-permitted.
sentences.i: And the morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent, leaving her permitted speech.
sentences.n: This is the night's closing formula, the same as at the end of the earlier nights: dawn catches Shahrazād in mid-tale, and she stops, to take up the story the next night.
